concepts.why: The patient presented with classic symptoms of appendicitis, including abdominal pain that localized to the right lower quadrant, nausea, and a positive Rovsing sign, and imaging studies showed inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve.
The patient has a history of endometriosis and biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis.
The patient developed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass.
The appendix was not identified on imaging studies and the patient had mild inflammatory changes of the terminal ileum and adhesions but no appendix.

rationales.F01: Abdominal pain is a non-specific symptom.
rationales.F02: Pain localization to the right lower quadrant is suggestive of appendicitis or inverted appendix.
rationales.F04: Tenderness in the right lower quadrant is consistent with appendicitis or small-bowel obstruction.
rationales.F05: Rovsing sign is indicative of appendicitis.
rationales.F07: Lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve is highly suggestive of appendicitis.
rationales.F08: The absence of an identified appendix suggests an inverted appendix or other conditions.
rationales.F09: Mild inflammatory changes and adhesions without an appendix are consistent with endometriosis or small-bowel obstruction.
rationales.F10: Biopsy demonstrating acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis supports the diagnosis of endometriosis.
rationales.F11: Elevated white-cell count is indicative of inflammation, consistent with appendicitis or small-bowel obstruction.
rationales.F12: Small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum is consistent with several conditions, including inverted appendix or small-bowel obstruction.

frontier_selector.rationale: Biopsy-confirmed foci of endometriosis with acute inflammation, explaining the patient's symptoms and findings, including the small-bowel obstruction likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass.
